main_text.p: tazalis, statuit Abu Motiai in libro الرد على ٭ اهل الثنوية البدع i.e. Responsionis ad Haereticos,) illos quos Althanawiah, i.e. duorum principiorum authores vocat, quorum sententia sit, ان الخير من الله والشر من ابليس ومن انفسنا Quòd bonum sit à Deo, malum autè à Diabolo & nobis ipsis. Motazalorum (plerorumq; saltem) sententia potiùs videtur liberam esse hominis sive ad bonum, sive malum potentiam, & ipsum actionum suarum dominum esse, ideoq; eos Magorum à reliquis Mohammedanorum sectis similes haberi, quòd alium à Deo actionum authorem statuunt. اتفقوا على ان العبد قادر خالق لافعاله خيرها وشرها مستحق على ما يفعله ثوابا وعقابا في الاخرة والرب تعالى منزه ان يضاف اليه شر وظلم وفعل هوكفر ومعصية لاذه[?] لو خلق الظلم كان ظالما كما لو خلق العدل كان عادلا (inquit Shareslanius) i.e. unanimi consensu statuunt, servum, i.e. hominem potentia praeditum esse, & creatorem esse actionum suarum tam bonarum quam malarum, ideoque dignum esse ob ea quae faciat, pramio vel poena in die judicii; Dominum autem procul ab hoc abesse ut attribuatur illi malum & iniquitas, & actio quae sit infidelitas & rebellio, quoniam si creares iniquitatem, iniquus esset, sicut si creces justitiam justus esl. Sed de eorum hac ex parte sententia plura dicendi mox dabitur occasio. Utri interim potiùs sectæ, Al Motazalorum (scil. qui decretum Dei tollunt, ut liberam homini in actiones suas potentiam tribuant,an Allabbarorum qui omnia

page.notes: Marginal note at right, beside the text: "In cap. de Al-Motaz." (printed in small type, hyphenated across lines). Left edge is cut, so the first word is a fragment: "tazalis," kept as printed. Arabic in the first lines is read with doubt: the opening line ("الرد على ٭ اهل") and the word لاذه (probably لانه) are not certain. The Arabic is set as printed in the scan. Italic spans in the Latin are approximate. Printed "creares" and "creces" and "esl." are kept as printed; "Responsionis" and "Althanawiah" as printed. The paragraph is cut off at the foot of the page and continues on the next page.
